## About Me

I'm a student at the **University of Essex** studying **Economics and Politics** (BSc). My academic work focuses on applying quantitative methods to understand political and social phenomena, with particular interests in electoral behavior, institutional trust, and data-driven policy analysis.

## Research Interests

My work in the **GV300 Research Methods** course has developed my capabilities in:

- **Causal Inference & Experimental Design** - A/B testing, treatment effect estimation, and randomized controlled trials
- **Statistical Modeling** - Linear and logistic regression, interaction effects, and heterogeneous treatment effects
- **Data Visualization** - Creating publication-quality graphics that communicate complex findings clearly
- **Text Analysis** - Natural language processing, sentiment analysis, and computational text methods
- **Reproducible Research** - R Markdown, Git/GitHub, and transparent analytical workflows

## Skills & Tools

**Programming & Analysis:**
- R (tidyverse, ggplot2, psych, tidytext, quanteda)
- RStudio and R Markdown for reproducible research
- Git and GitHub for version control

**Statistical Methods:**
- Regression analysis (OLS, logistic)
- Experimental design and causal inference
- Measurement theory and scale construction
- Text analysis and natural language processing

**Data Visualization:**
- ggplot2 for publication-quality graphics
- Interactive visualizations
- Effective communication of quantitative findings

## Portfolio

**[GV300 Quantitative Analysis →](gv300-showcase.html)**  
Examples of statistical modeling, experimental design, and data visualization from my research methods coursework, including:

- A/B testing for political communications

**[Text Analysis Showcase →](text-analysis.html)**  
Demonstrations of computational text analysis methods including sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and text classification applied to political texts and social media data.
